transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-29
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE); Marcus Chen (Redwood SE); Priya Nair (AuroraCloud PM); Owen Blake (Cloud Eng); Marta Ruiz (Solution Architect)

[00:00:00] Lena Ortiz: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick round robin, I think we all have this on calendar to sync on the marketplace listing and the reference architecture for the joint solution.
[00:00:23] Priya Nair: Yep, thanks Lena. We're excited to get the AuroraCloud listing live and make sure the ref arch shows both the managed hosted flow and the private VPC option for larger customers.
[00:00:45] Marcus Chen: Awesome. I can kick off with the high level tech constraints we saw in the last email - things like KMS integration, VPC peering, and the Dedicated GPU pool sizing for inference.
[00:01:10] Owen Blake: Quick note: our compliance team wants to see SOC2 and at-rest encryption details. Also any HSM/KMS flow for key custody - we have strict requirements.
[00:01:35] Marta Ruiz: And we need a reference arch that shows fallbacks for capacity - like Redwood hosted -> Dedicated -> private on-prem, something that maps to our customer SLAs.
[00:02:05] Lena Ortiz: Right. From Redwood's side, we can show the three deployment modes. Quick caveat, sometimes the transcription in our docs calls Redwood Dedicated weirdly, we've seen "Redwood Dedicate" in exports, but techwise it's the Reserved GPU pools.
[00:02:30] Marcus Chen: (laughs) yeah, those typos... For the diagram I'll include the runtime pieces: serving runtime with KV cache, compilation/kernel selection, and smart routing. We'll also mark where caching happens for shared tenancy vs dedicated.
[00:02:58] Priya Nair: Can you also highlight networking flows? We need the exact ports and whether the control plane requires outbound access to Redwood. Some of our customers are air-gapped.
[00:03:22] Marcus Chen: Absolutely. We'll call out control plane traffic and the optional private control plane for Aurora's on-prem customers. For air-gapped, that's the Private (on-prem) installation path.
[00:03:48] Owen Blake: For marketplace listing specifically, what metadata do you need? pricing SKU, image references, deploy scripts?
[00:04:05] Lena Ortiz: Good question. We'll send a checklist but high level: SKU definitions (hosted vs dedicated vs private), supported regions, resource footprints (vCPU/GPU memory), expected throughput baselines, and required env vars/secrets like KMS identifiers. Also a short usage guide and a reference Helm chart or ARM template.
[00:04:34] Marta Ruiz: Do you have a preferred format for the reference arch artefact? PNG + architecture markdown would be easiest for us.
[00:04:46] Marcus Chen: PNG for the diagram + a markdown doc that has the sequence flows and config snippets. We'll include a sample values.yaml for the helm chart.
[00:05:10] Priya Nair: Security questions - SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs. How much detail do you need on the audit log schema?
[00:05:25] Lena Ortiz: A summary in the marketplace listing is fine, but for enterprise customers we should be able to attach our security pack - the SOC2 report and the audit log schema. We'll share the security docs once you sign the mutual NDA or sign the access request.
[00:05:50] Owen Blake: Sounds good. Also, can you confirm whether token-level billing is exposed via the marketplace or we need to handle metering on our side?
[00:06:05] Marcus Chen: Billing exposure depends on the marketplace. For Cloud marketplaces that support metered billing, we can surface token-level metrics; otherwise we'll provide usage export hooks and you can ingest them into your billing. We'll document both options.
[00:06:30] Priya Nair: Good. On the integration testing front, we can provide a test tenant. We will need guidance on expected request patterns so we can provision adequate GPU capacity for the POC.
[00:06:48] Lena Ortiz: Marcus, can you write up the expected workload profile? Typical seq lengths, concurrency, batching expectations, and KV cache hit rates?
[00:07:05] Marcus Chen: Sure - I'll draft a starter profile. Example: 1) chat API typical seq length 128 tokens, burst concurrency 50 req/s, RTT SLO 150-300ms for hosted, 2) embeddings batch throughput targets. I'll include sample load generator scripts.
[00:07:35] Marta Ruiz: Will you include quantization/precision recommendations? Some of our infra teams prefer int8 Q4 ops for cost savings.
[00:07:48] Marcus Chen: Yes, we'll call out model/quantization profiles and tradeoffs. For certain models we recommend int8 for inference on Dedicated, but note some quality regression risk - we'll include eval metrics.
[00:08:12] Priya Nair: About the reference arch, can we show a fallback policy in the diagram? So if Dedicated capacity exhausted, we can route to hosted with reduced batch sizes.
[00:08:28] Marcus Chen: Definitely - smart routing with fallbacks is a Redwood feature. We'll diagram routing policies: latency-first, cost-first, and region affinity, and show automatic fallback to compatible model variants.
[00:08:52] Lena Ortiz: Switching to marketplace ops: do you have an expected launch timeline? Priya?
[00:09:03] Priya Nair: We'd like to target a closed alpha in mid-May and GA in early June, assuming integration testing goes well. So ideally we get the reference arch and the listing checklist by first week of May.
[00:09:22] Lena Ortiz: Great - that aligns with our PM calendar. Marcus, that means diagram by 2026-05-06, and I'll send the listing checklist by 2026-05-04.
[00:09:35] Owen Blake: On the technical requirements, what about Kubernetes versions and supported node types? Our platform is on 1.26 clusters and we use mixed instance types.
[00:09:52] Marcus Chen: We'll include a compatibility matrix - supported K8s versions, helm chart requirements, and recommended instance families for GPU inference (e.g., A100, H100 alternatives with notes on kernel support).
[00:10:20] Marta Ruiz: Any dependencies on Redis/kv stores for caching? We prefer not to add more managed services if possible.
[00:10:33] Marcus Chen: Redwood's KV cache is an internal runtime concept; for private deployments we support an optional external Redis backing for persistence. We'll mark that as optional but show recommended configs.
[00:10:55] Priya Nair: Good to know. One more security ask: our legal wants to confirm data residency options - can customers force request processing only in region X?
[00:11:08] Lena Ortiz: Yes, region pinning is supported. We'll include region-level routing policies in the doc. For on-prem/air-gapped customers, the Private install keeps everything in-customer.
[00:11:28] Owen Blake: Cool. About monitoring and observability - we want to surface per-route latency and token-level cost. Can Redwood export to Prometheus or do you push metrics?
[00:11:41] Marcus Chen: Both. We'll provide Prometheus exporters in the on-prem package and a metrics export API for hosted customers. We'll also include sample Grafana dashboards.
[00:12:02] Priya Nair: For the marketplace listing copy, do you have a boilerplate we can reuse?
[00:12:08] Lena Ortiz: Yes, we'll provide a short product description, feature bullets, and a few screenshots. I'll send the boilerplate in the marketplace checklist.
[00:12:23] Marta Ruiz: Are there known limitations we should call out for customers? Like max sequence length supported for certain quantized models?
[00:12:35] Marcus Chen: We'll include a limitations section - e.g., quantized int8 models may have a smaller max sequence length or different kernel support. Also GPU memory limits for large context windows.
[00:12:58] Lena Ortiz: Let's capture next steps and owners. (brief pause)
[00:13:10] Priya Nair: Quick question - any competitors doing similar marketplace integrations? We referenced Cloudpeak earlier, they have a listing but limited private deploy options.
[00:13:25] Lena Ortiz: Right, Cloudpeak offers hosted but their private story is weaker; NovaEdge has a stronger on-prem push. We'll emphasize our unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private as the differentiator.
[00:13:45] Owen Blake: For the POC, do you require any contract or is the alpha on a trial credit basis?
[00:13:55] Lena Ortiz: For partners we can offer trial credits for early testing; we'll follow up on contracting with the partnerships team.
[00:14:10] Marcus Chen: I'll note any port numbers and sample env vars in the ref arch doc. Also include a minimal helm values example for quick deploy.
[00:14:28] Priya Nair: Great - and I'll coordinate test account creation with Owen.
[00:14:40] Marta Ruiz: One operational detail: do you support rolling upgrades without KV cache blowups?
[00:14:51] Marcus Chen: Yes, the runtime supports warm KV cache migration and graceful rollouts; we'll include a note on canary strategies in the reference arch.
[00:15:12] Lena Ortiz: Nice. I think that's most of the tech asks. Anything else from AuroraCloud?
[00:15:21] Priya Nair: Nothing major. Just that we'll need to review the SOC2 docs before GA.
[00:15:30] Lena Ortiz: Understood. I'll include the security pack link in the follow-up email and indicate redacted artifacts for initial review.
[00:15:44] Owen Blake: OK. Timeline recap - reference arch + integration notes by Marcus 2026-05-06, checklist + marketplace boilerplate from Lena 2026-05-04, Aurora to provide test tenancy/access by 2026-05-11, follow-up integration test review 2026-05-20.
[00:16:05] Marcus Chen: I'll also add a sample perf spreadsheet with expected token/sec and latency numbers.
[00:16:18] Marta Ruiz: We'll validate and share any infra gaps by 2026-05-18.
[00:16:30] Lena Ortiz: Perfect. If no other questions, we'll wrap. Thanks everyone.
[00:16:36] Priya Nair: Thanks all.
[00:16:38] Owen Blake: Thanks.
[00:16:40] Marta Ruiz: Bye.
[00:56:50] (end of call)

Notes: occasional transcription errors observed in product names and acronyms; action items listed above. References shared during call: link to marketplace checklist (internal doc), sample Helm chart (repo link), security pack (link placeholder).
